name: Synth-native noise air: noise osc on its own low-pass with a fast envelope for bright attack, shelved tape-noise bed boosted near 6 kHz, +24 st noise layer on bass, envelope-following tuned noise on drums, parallel master noise chain
goal: Add air and 'fidelity' with noise generated or layered inside the patch instead of opening the main filter (which adds unwanted energy). Core recipe: put noise on oscillator 2, route oscillators to separate filters (split routing), low-pass the noise and drive its cutoff from a sharp, fast envelope so it adds only a bright, breathy attack. Supporting layers: a low-shelved tape-noise bed with a bell boost near 6 kHz, sneaked in until barely noticed; a noise sampler on the bass MIDI transposed +24 st with a short decay at about -8 dB; envelope-following narrow-band noise on kick (~5 kHz) and snare (~7 kHz, decorrelated for width); and a parallel master noise chain after the other master FX with slow, unsynced, out-of-phase filter LFOs. Delta vs brightness-and-air variants (start-bright-then-filter, field-recording HPF+exciter): this one makes the air from noise inside the synth/patch and on each element.

source.title: How to Use White Noise in Your Music

prerequisites: A synth with a noise oscillator (or noise wavetable), two filters with split/parallel routing, and a second envelope
A sampler that can play a noise sample from MIDI; EQ; an envelope-follower or gate-keyed noise source; a delay or noise generator for the master chain
Clean noise sources (white/pink/tape hiss) without crackle or vinyl clicks

inputs.name: pad_or_lead_patch
inputs.description: Patch whose attack should get brighter without opening the main filter

inputs.name: bass_track
inputs.description: Bass part that can take a parallel noise layer

inputs.name: drum_hits
inputs.description: Kick and snare to receive tuned noise

outputs.name: air_patch
outputs.description: Patch with an envelope-shaped noise attack on its own filter

outputs.name: noise_layers
outputs.description: Noise bed, bass noise layer, drum noise and master noise chain, each sitting just below notice

constraints: Pick hiss without crackle or random clicks; the source notes tape noise can carry random clicks, which Matt dislikes. High-pass or swap the sample if clicks are audible.
Demo levels in the source were exaggerated on purpose; final noise levels should be just noticeable on A/B, not obvious.
Use a low shelf rather than a steep low cut on the noise bed (per the source), then boost a pleasing band near 6 kHz.
Avoid audio-rate or random modulation on the noise layers; slow, steady LFOs only.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Noise bed: put a long tape-hiss/white-noise sample on its own track and hold one note for the whole section. Add an EQ with a low shelf turned down to clear masking lows (shelf, not a steep low cut), then a smooth bell boost around 6 kHz (the 'brilliance' range) where the noise sounds pleasant.
steps.expect: Noise bed with only a bright, airy top

steps.action: Pull the bed way down, then raise it until you just notice it. A/B: without it the mix should sound 'clinical/lifeless'; with it, a little fidelity comes back.
steps.expect: Bed is felt more than heard

steps.action: Synth-native air: in the pad/lead patch, turn on oscillator 2 with a noise wave. Set filter routing to split so osc 1 goes to filter 1 and the noise osc goes to filter 2.
steps.expect: Noise processed separately from the tonal osc

steps.action: Set filter 2 to low-pass. Give envelope 2 a sharp spike (fast attack, short decay, no sustain) and route it to filter 2 cutoff in the mod matrix. Lower filter 2's base cutoff until the noise is heard only as a bright, breathy attack, not a steady hiss. Turn resonance down.
steps.expect: Brighter attack without opening the main filter

steps.action: Raise the envelope-to-cutoff amount for more punch, and back off the noise osc level so it isn't detectable as noise. Optionally automate the noise level up over a section as a slow, rising energy element.
steps.expect: Attack brightness that can grow across the track

steps.action: Bass noise layer: group the bass chain and add a parallel chain with a white-noise sample in a sampler, fed by the same MIDI. Add a pitch MIDI effect of +24 semitones so the noise sits two octaves up and its colour follows the notes. Set amp envelope sustain to 0 and tune decay to a short burst; mix it at about -8 dB.
steps.expect: Bass gains a little upper 'oomph' that tracks each note

steps.action: Drums: put an envelope-following tuned-noise device (noise shaped by the input's envelope, narrow band-pass; Erosion-like) on the kick around 5 kHz for snap, and on the snare around 7 kHz. For the snare, switch to decorrelated/wide noise (different L/R) for a stereo burst. The peak level rises, so turn the track down to keep limiter headroom.
steps.expect: Snappier kick, brighter and wider snare without new samples

steps.action: Master noise: make a parallel rack on the master after the other master FX, with a dry chain and a noise chain. In the noise chain, use a noise generator (e.g. a delay's noise feature) with input at about -40 dB or none. Filter the noise and modulate the two filters with slow, unsynced LFOs set out of phase with each other, plus an optional small resonant hump. Sneak it in.
steps.tool: Parallel master chain + filtered noise + slow LFOs
steps.expect: Gently moving air bed that later EQ doesn't boost

steps.action: Map every noise addition to one mute/macro key and A/B the full mix with and without the noise.
steps.expect: Subtle, consistent improvement in perceived fidelity

verification: With noise layers muted the mix sounds duller/'clinical'; enabled at final level, the change is subtle but audible.
Pad attack is brighter while the main filter cutoff is unchanged (noise only on filter 2).
No audible crackle/clicks in the noise bed; master noise sits after other master FX.
Bass noise layer sits about 8 dB under the bass and decays quickly (sustain 0).
